title: Korea job intelligence - discovery
description: What the pipeline has found, read against the three things this project is for: engineering roles at smaller employers, engineering roles in finance, and everything else. The ingestion dashboard next to this one answers whether the pipeline is working; this one answers what it found.

panels.title: Open postings
panels.description: Everything not closed on recorded evidence.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS value FROM jobs j WHERE j.lifecycle_state <> 'CLOSED'

panels.title: At smaller employers
panels.description: Open postings whose employer is not one of the recognised big names. Null stage means unassessed, not small — this counts both.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS value FROM jobs j JOIN companies c ON c.id = j.company_id WHERE j.lifecycle_state <> 'CLOSED' AND (c.stage IS NULL OR c.stage <> 'LARGE')

panels.title: In a financial sector
panels.description: Fintech, banking, securities, crypto or insurance.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS value FROM jobs j WHERE j.lifecycle_state <> 'CLOSED' AND j.sector IN ('FINTECH','BANKING','SECURITIES','CRYPTO','INSURANCE')

panels.title: Junior accessible
panels.description: Seniority A or B. C and above are excluded, and an unestablished seniority is not counted as junior.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS value FROM jobs j WHERE j.lifecycle_state <> 'CLOSED' AND j.seniority_bucket IN ('A','B')

panels.title: 1 - Hidden gems: engineering at smaller employers
Open engineering roles at employers that are not big names
panels.description: Ordered by career value, then by how recently the posting was first seen. A role family of null means the classifier found no evidence, so those rows are excluded rather than guessed at — widen the filter below if you want them.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  c.canonical_name AS "Employer",
  j.canonical_title AS "Role",
  lower(j.role_family) AS "Family",
  coalesce(lower(j.sector), '') AS "Sector",
  j.seniority_bucket AS "Sen",
  j.career_value_score AS "SWE",
  coalesce(j.location_city, j.location_raw) AS "Location",
  j.first_seen_at AS "First seen"
FROM jobs j
JOIN companies c ON c.id = j.company_id
WHERE j.lifecycle_state <> 'CLOSED' AND (c.stage IS NULL OR c.stage <> 'LARGE') AND j.role_family IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY j.career_value_score DESC NULLS LAST, j.first_seen_at DESC
LIMIT 200

panels.title: Smaller employers by open postings
panels.description: How deep the coverage of each employer is. A long tail of ones is what shallow discovery looks like: the employer was found, its board was not read.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT c.canonical_name AS "Employer", count(*)::int AS "Open postings"
FROM jobs j JOIN companies c ON c.id = j.company_id
WHERE j.lifecycle_state <> 'CLOSED' AND (c.stage IS NULL OR c.stage <> 'LARGE')
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC, 1 LIMIT 25

panels.title: How many employers sit at each depth
panels.description: Employers bucketed by how many open postings each has. A spike at one is the signal that discovery is finding names rather than boards.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT depth::text AS "Open postings per employer", count(*)::int AS "Employers"
FROM (
  SELECT c.id, count(*) AS depth
  FROM jobs j JOIN companies c ON c.id = j.company_id
  WHERE j.lifecycle_state <> 'CLOSED' AND (c.stage IS NULL OR c.stage <> 'LARGE')
  GROUP BY c.id
) per_employer
GROUP BY depth ORDER BY depth

panels.title: Open roles in a financial sector
panels.description: Sector is assigned from the employer first and the title second; the description is deliberately not consulted, because it named the wrong industry more often than the right one. Confidence sits with the extracted field on the job's own page.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  c.canonical_name AS "Employer",
  j.canonical_title AS "Role",
  lower(j.sector) AS "Sector",
  coalesce(lower(j.role_family), '') AS "Family",
  j.seniority_bucket AS "Sen",
  j.career_value_score AS "SWE",
  coalesce(c.stage, '') AS "Employer size",
  coalesce(j.location_city, j.location_raw) AS "Location"
FROM jobs j
JOIN companies c ON c.id = j.company_id
WHERE j.lifecycle_state <> 'CLOSED' AND j.sector IN ('FINTECH','BANKING','SECURITIES','CRYPTO','INSURANCE')
ORDER BY j.career_value_score DESC NULLS LAST, c.canonical_name
LIMIT 200

panels.title: Financial postings by sector
panels.description: Five sectors are treated as financial. Which one a posting landed in is intelligence, not a filter anyone should have to know to ask the question.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT lower(j.sector) AS "Sector", count(*)::int AS "Open postings"
FROM jobs j WHERE j.lifecycle_state <> 'CLOSED' AND j.sector IN ('FINTECH','BANKING','SECURITIES','CRYPTO','INSURANCE')
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Financial postings by employer size
panels.description: Whether the financial roles found are concentrated in the big names or spread wider.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT coalesce(c.stage, 'unassessed') AS "Employer size", count(*)::int AS "Open postings"
FROM jobs j JOIN companies c ON c.id = j.company_id
WHERE j.lifecycle_state <> 'CLOSED' AND j.sector IN ('FINTECH','BANKING','SECURITIES','CRYPTO','INSURANCE')
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Open postings by role family
panels.description: Only postings the classifier could place. Roughly three in four carry no role family, which is the extraction gap rather than a shortage of engineering roles.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT lower(j.role_family) AS "Role family", count(*)::int AS "Open postings"
FROM jobs j WHERE j.lifecycle_state <> 'CLOSED' AND j.role_family IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Open postings by seniority
panels.description: A and B are the junior-accessible buckets. Unestablished is shown as its own bar rather than folded into a neighbour.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT coalesce(j.seniority_bucket, 'unestablished') AS "Seniority", count(*)::int AS "Open postings"
FROM jobs j WHERE j.lifecycle_state <> 'CLOSED'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Highest career value outside the financial sectors
panels.description: The rest of the engineering market, ranked the same way.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  c.canonical_name AS "Employer",
  j.canonical_title AS "Role",
  lower(j.role_family) AS "Family",
  coalesce(lower(j.sector), '') AS "Sector",
  j.seniority_bucket AS "Sen",
  j.career_value_score AS "SWE",
  j.application_priority_score AS "Priority",
  coalesce(j.location_city, j.location_raw) AS "Location"
FROM jobs j
JOIN companies c ON c.id = j.company_id
WHERE j.lifecycle_state <> 'CLOSED' AND j.role_family IS NOT NULL
  AND (j.sector IS NULL OR j.sector NOT IN ('FINTECH','BANKING','SECURITIES','CRYPTO','INSURANCE'))
ORDER BY j.career_value_score DESC NULLS LAST, j.application_priority_score DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 200

panels.title: Postings first seen per day, by source
panels.description: Counted against the job's first sighting, so a posting is attributed to whichever source found it first and never counted twice.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  date_trunc('day', j.first_seen_at) AS time,
  s.code AS metric,
  count(DISTINCT j.id)::int AS value
FROM jobs j
JOIN job_sources js ON js.job_id = j.id
JOIN sources s ON s.id = js.source_id
WHERE $__timeFilter(j.first_seen_at)
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: What each source is contributing
panels.description: Provider rows against distinct jobs. A source whose two numbers are far apart is either corroborating what another source already found or repeating itself.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  s.code AS "Source",
  s.adapter_kind AS "Adapter",
  count(*)::int AS "Provider rows",
  count(DISTINCT js.job_id)::int AS "Distinct jobs",
  count(DISTINCT j.company_id)::int AS "Employers",
  sum((j.lifecycle_state <> 'CLOSED')::int)::int AS "Still open",
  max(js.last_seen_at) AS "Last seen"
FROM job_sources js
JOIN sources s ON s.id = js.source_id
JOIN jobs j ON j.id = js.job_id
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 4 DESC

panels.title: Employers the console has not sized
panels.description: Stage is recorded only on evidence: a lexicon name match, or the employer running its own board. Everything here is unassessed, which is not the same as small.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  c.canonical_name AS "Employer",
  count(*)::int AS "Open postings",
  count(DISTINCT js.source_id)::int AS "Sources",
  min(j.first_seen_at) AS "First seen"
FROM companies c
JOIN jobs j ON j.company_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN job_sources js ON js.job_id = j.id
WHERE c.stage IS NULL AND j.lifecycle_state <> 'CLOSED'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC, 1 LIMIT 100
